content: Both ligands are poor and neither is active: ligand 1 is a 475 Da tetracyclic imide with QED 0.290 and LogP 5.34, ligand 2 a 450 Da thienopyrimidine amide at QED 0.596. Crossover between them would just produce another large, greasy molecule. But ligand 1 contains one genuinely useful piece: the N-aryl ring at atoms 20-23, 25 and 30, a benzene whose carbon 20 is attached to the imide nitrogen at atom 19, with a chlorine at carbon 23 - para to 20 - and a trifluoromethyl at carbon 25. If I anchor on the aryl carbon and cut toward the imide nitrogen, I keep that ring and discard the entire fused core in one modification: 26 atoms gone. In its place I attach 4-cyclopropylpyridin-2-ylamino. The 4-methyl on this pyridine was worth about +0.13, so the open question is how far that alkyl can grow; a cyclopropyl is the largest I will try, and it is a group that tends to help drug-likeness rather than hurt it.
